title: A durable, implantable artificial kidney

concept.text: A durable, implantable artificial kidney would be a manufactured device placed inside the body that continuously provides sufficient kidney replacement to sustain a person with kidney failure. It would remove appropriate wastes and excess water while maintaining fluid and electrolyte balance, with reliable operation over long periods. The defining advance is an integrated replacement system; an isolated blood filter or a short-lived compartment of kidney cells would demonstrate only part of that capability.

One proposed route combines a hemofilter with a bioreactor containing living renal cells. The filter produces an ultrafiltrate from blood, and the cell compartment would process that fluid, recovering needed water and sodium while directing remaining waste toward the bladder. Silicon nanopore membranes are intended to support exchange while protecting the cells from immune attack. This bioartificial architecture illustrates the concept, but the innovation ultimately depends on sustained replacement function and safety rather than on any single component design.

significance.text: If achieved, sustained kidney replacement from a fully implanted manufactured system would provide a fundamentally different treatment option for kidney failure. A recipient could obtain continuous replacement without recurring maintenance dialysis sessions or a donor kidney. This would address two major constraints motivating the research: the burden and incomplete functional replacement of hemodialysis, and the limited availability of transplant organs.

Conditional impact synthesis: successful deployment could reduce dependence on donor supply and dialysis infrastructure, but the scale of that effect would depend on manufacturing capacity, affordability, surgical access, device durability and adoption. An implant could also shift care toward implantation, monitoring, maintenance and eventual replacement. Better quality of life, improved clinical outcomes and lower total costs are possibilities to test, rather than automatic consequences of putting treatment inside the body.

The analogy to a natural kidney has important limits. Demonstrating filtration, tubular processing or dialysis independence would not by itself establish that the implant reproduces every renal function. Endocrine sufficiency and the need for continuing medicines or other supplementation would require separate evaluation. The supplied component study does not establish complete physiological replacement or clinical superiority.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central capability still to be established by the supplied evidence is durable integration: coupling filtration to sufficient downstream fluid processing and waste excretion in one implanted system. A filter must deliver an appropriate ultrafiltrate, and the processing compartment must recover needed substances and water at rates sufficient for kidney replacement. Cell survival or expression of renal genes alone cannot establish that the combined system provides adequate transport, clearance or life support.

Long-term operation also requires a safe interface with blood and surrounding tissues. Concrete barriers include thrombosis, infection, loss of device integrity and sustained compatibility of the membranes and vascular connections. For a living-cell design, enough cells must remain viable and functionally active while being protected from immune attack. The 2023 paper identifies increased cell numbers, longer implantation periods and testing in animals with reduced renal function as future steps; its short implants do not establish that these requirements can be maintained for years.

Engineering synthesis: a practical implant would also need reproducible manufacture, consistent functional performance, monitoring that detects deterioration, and workable procedures for maintenance or replacement. Its operating limits would need definition, including how it handles changing fluid and electrolyte demands and which functions require supplementation. These are requirements for translating a successful prototype into durable treatment, not capabilities demonstrated in the supplied study.

current_state.text: Kim and colleagues reported a bioreactor component study in Nature Communications on August 29, 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-39888-2. They implanted a human renal-cell bioreactor in five healthy female adolescent Yucatan minipigs: three implants lasted three days and two lasted seven days. The experiment demonstrated short-term feasibility of an implanted cell compartment. It did not test an integrated hemofilter–bioreactor system providing life-sustaining replacement in animals with kidney failure.

The animals received no immunosuppression and no ongoing systemic anticoagulation. They did receive aspirin and clopidogrel through device retrieval, as well as an intraoperative intravenous heparin dose of 100 units/kg before vessel occlusion. This distinction matters: the study supports short-term implantation under that specific drug regimen, rather than implantation with no antithrombotic treatment or no exposure to anticoagulants.

Functional evidence principally concerned cell viability and gene-expression surrogates. These observations support further development, but they do not establish replacement-level transport or clearance. The healthy animals retained their own kidney function, so their survival cannot demonstrate that the bioreactor could sustain a recipient with kidney failure. Longer implantation, functional transport testing, greater cell capacity and integration remained future work in the paper.

Evidence boundary: the supplied review reports complete text extraction across the article's 11 pages, with no recorded extraction issues or truncation. Linked supplementary material was not included in that review, and its conclusions did not require inspection of figure images. The supplied evidence therefore supports this dated 2023 result within those limits. No freshness search was supplied to establish the latest state as of November 2026; that limitation does not show that subsequent advances have or have not occurred.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: a fully implanted integrated system should sustain people with kidney failure without maintenance dialysis for years, with acceptable complications and quality of life. A clinical protocol would need to define those outcomes prospectively, including the handling of rescue dialysis, device revisions and treatment discontinuation. The years-long endpoint is a proposed test of durability, not an established standard or a result reported by the supplied source.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed functional evidence: demonstrate adequate waste removal, water balance and electrolyte regulation under clinically relevant conditions, with direct measurements of integrated performance. For a cell-based device, confirm sustained transport function as well as cell viability. Identify essential functions the implant supplies and those managed by supplementation, including any endocrine needs, so that dialysis independence is not mistaken for complete replication of a natural kidney.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed functional evidence

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: reproduce performance across independently manufactured devices, clinical teams and a defined range of patients. Follow recipients long enough to characterize thrombosis, infection, immune injury where relevant, mechanical failures, medication requirements and replacement procedures. Assess manufacturing consistency, maintenance burden and patient-reported outcomes. Such finite studies would establish demonstrated breadth and durability within their tested populations and conditions, rather than literal universality or unlimited device life.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: NEP-01, “Regrow functional nephrons inside an adult human kidney,” and NEP-02, “Rebuild function in scarred kidneys by reversing established fibrosis,” seek to restore the patient's existing kidneys. NEP-04 instead supplies replacement through an implanted manufactured system. Living renal cells could contribute to either approach, but regeneration within native tissue and operation inside a device remain distinct capabilities.

Roster-based synthesis: NEP-03, “Manufacture transplantable human kidneys from cells,” shares the goal of creating replacement capacity without relying on conventional donor supply. Its defining product is a transplantable human kidney, whereas NEP-04 is an artificial or bioartificial device that may combine engineered membranes with cells. NEP-06, “An effectively unlimited supply of durable animal-donor kidneys,” pursues another replacement route through animal organs. Each route has different requirements for production, implantation, compatibility and durability.

Roster-based synthesis: NEP-05, “Kidney replacement that is portable and affordable at global scale,” overlaps with the freedom from recurring facility-based treatment that an implant might offer. Its defining requirements are portability, affordability and broad access; NEP-04 specifically requires durable implantation. An implant could be expensive or difficult to maintain, while a portable replacement system could remain outside the body. Neither concept's success automatically establishes the other.

Roster-based synthesis: NEP-07, “Reliably induce donor-specific tolerance in kidney recipients,” concerns acceptance of donor tissue. It overlaps with the immune-protection challenge of a cell-containing artificial kidney, but membrane-based protection of cells inside a device is distinct from inducing donor-specific immune tolerance. The bioreactor's short-term use without immunosuppression does not demonstrate transplantation tolerance.

Roster-based synthesis: NEP-08, “A root-cause, durable treatment for ADPKD,” NEP-09, “Durable reversal of diabetic kidney disease,” and NEP-10, “Broad prevention of severe acute kidney injury,” aim to treat underlying disease or prevent kidney damage. Their success could reduce the need for replacement. NEP-04 addresses loss of kidney function after replacement becomes necessary; providing that function does not itself demonstrate treatment of those underlying causes.

change_log.change: Preserved NEP-04's identity and expanded its explanation around integrated filtration, tubular processing, fluid recovery and waste excretion.
change_log.reason: The research and review identify durable integrated replacement as the innovation, with the bioreactor serving as one enabling component.

change_log.change: Dated the component result to August 29, 2023, and specified five healthy minipigs, with three three-day implants and two seven-day implants.
change_log.reason: The reviewed methods support these details and limit extrapolation to longer implantation or recipients with kidney failure.

change_log.change: Disclosed intraoperative intravenous heparin at 100 units/kg alongside aspirin, clopidogrel and the absence of ongoing systemic anticoagulation.
change_log.reason: The original wording could obscure the documented surgical anticoagulant exposure.

change_log.change: Distinguished viability and gene-expression evidence from replacement-level transport, clearance and life support.
change_log.reason: The reviewed findings support component feasibility without establishing integrated renal replacement.

change_log.change: Retained the revolutionary potential while separating direct treatment consequences from conditional infrastructure, cost and outcome benefits.
change_log.reason: The replacement capability supports the former; the latter require evidence about durability, deployment, access and clinical performance.

change_log.change: Made the proposed completion criteria explicit and added reproducibility, measurable outcomes and practical operating boundaries.
change_log.reason: The years-long human endpoint is coherent but is not a published standard; finite demonstrations establish performance only within tested conditions.

change_log.change: Preserved the review's full-text, supplementary-material and freshness limitations, and paraphrased the earlier non-verbatim quotation.
change_log.reason: Source coverage must not imply inspection beyond the supplied review or verification of the latest state in November 2026.

change_log.change: Explained overlap and distinctions with every other supplied roster entry.
change_log.reason: Shared goals or enabling technologies do not make regeneration, organ manufacture, portability, tolerance and disease prevention the same innovation.

unresolved_issues: The latest development state as of November 2026 cannot be established from the supplied 2023 article and empty freshness record.
The reviewed evidence does not establish integrated replacement-level transport, dialysis independence or long-term performance in kidney failure.
Long-term cell function, immune protection, hemocompatibility, infection risk and device integrity remain unestablished by these short-duration implants.
Linked supplementary material was outside the supplied review; its potential contribution is not resolved here.
Endocrine sufficiency, supplementation needs, affordability, clinical superiority and scalable manufacture remain to be demonstrated.
The proposed human completion endpoint still requires measurable acceptance criteria, a defined patient population, follow-up duration and rules for rescue treatment or device revision.
